rationale: Counting how many pictures among several satisfy a given property (built from exactly 8 triangles); no existing slug covers counting matching figures across options.
Counting one object type in a busy picture that also has distractor objects (bones); not a tally-marks or triangle-in-figure count.
Adding days across a month boundary to find a matching calendar date; distinct from clock-time-after (hours/minutes) with no date/month concept in the set.
Tracking which digit first appears latest while listing a count-by-N sequence; different from digit-frequency (counting occurrences).
Finding the most frequently occurring picture/item across a grid of pictures; no existing mode/frequency-of-pictures concept.
Overlapping circles each sum to the same constant; solve for two unknown regions. Distinct from weight-balance-word (no items/weights, just circle-region sums).
Fill 1-9 uniquely into a 3x3 grid using given row/column sum clues (sudoku-like); no existing slug for unique-digit grid with row/col sum constraints.
Reading a cyclic colour ring and matching it to a straight strip that can be rotated but not flipped; distinct from same-figure-identify (single shape rotation, not colour sequences).

Following a chain of directional arrows with step counts through a grid to an exit; different from grid-path-steps/maze-path-shortest which are about shortest paths, not following prescribed arrow instructions.
Finding the maximum number of non-overlapping adjacent-square groups summing to a target in a number grid; a packing/optimization task not covered by any existing concept.

Folding a labelled net into a cube and finding max/min sum of three faces meeting at a vertex (avoiding opposite-face pairs); distinct from dice-opposite-faces (fixed 7-sum die) and dice-net-fold (choosing a valid net).
Marking cells in a grid by divisibility (multiples of 3/5/8) and counting full rows/columns/diagonals of matching marks; a distinct combined divisibility+grid-line-counting task.
Using the sum of Monday dates in a month to deduce the first Monday, then find the weekday of another date; calendar/weekday deduction not covered by clock-time-after.
Overlapping circles with a fixed per-circle total, solving for two unknown regions.
Unique 1-9 grid fill with row/column sum clues outside the grid, solving for two marked cells' sum.
Following arrows with directions and step counts across a grid from a start icon to an exit fruit.
Matching a cyclic colour ring's order to a straight strip allowing rotation but not flipping.

Solving a small system of symbol equations (triangle, circle, square) via root/division/substitution, then evaluating a combined expression; not covered by combination-product-sum (two-number sum/product) or custom-operation (new operator definition).
Maximum count of non-overlapping L/line-shaped trios summing to a target across a number grid.
Ordering three angles by visual opening width; angle-type only covers classifying a single angle's type (acute/right/obtuse), not comparing/ordering multiple angles.
Computing and comparing perimeters of several differently-shaped figures (rectangle, triangle, square) with cancelling arcs; broader than the single-shape shape-perimeter-square/rectangle concepts.
Folding a net into a cube and finding the minimum sum of three faces meeting at a vertex.
A vertical multiplication with hidden digit boxes; find all valid digit assignments then combine max/min. Distinct from build-number-from-digit-clues (position clues, not a multiplication check).
Counting 4-digit numbers whose digits satisfy a total-sum constraint plus a ratio relationship between digit-group sums; beyond simple digit-sum (which just computes one number's digit sum).
Marking a 5x5 grid by divisibility (3/5/8) and counting full lines of matching symbols.
Transforming a 3D cube solid layer-by-layer using an add/remove table, then matching the resulting shape; distinct from the 2D shape-transformation-rule (rotate/flip).
Solving symbol equations (triangle, circle, square) via cube-root/division, then substituting into a final expression.
Pigeonhole-principle problem: minimum picks from a numbered set to guarantee two numbers summing to a target; no combinatorial-guarantee concept exists in the set.
Unique 1-9 grid fill using row/column sum clues, solving for three marked cells.
Repeatedly applying a last-two-digits operation many times and using cycle detection to find a far-future term; distinct from digit-frequency and pattern-next.
Using given block areas and widths to algebraically solve for an unknown band's value; a composite area/algebra task beyond simple rectangle-area concepts.
A 1-4 sudoku variant where each cell has forbidden-digit corner clues; solve and sum shaded cells. Distinct puzzle mechanic from the 1-9 sum-clue grids.
Summing a mixed collection of bills/coins shown in a picture to a grand total; distinct from money-coins-total (cents needed to reach 100) and money-shopping-change (change after a purchase).
Comparing total stroke/line length across letters/shapes drawn on a grid; not covered by shape-perimeter concepts (which are for simple polygons).
Counting two different shape types (circles vs rectangles) across several pictures and comparing which wins; distinct from count-polygon-sides and count-shapes-in-figure (single shape type).

Finding a subset of labelled values that sums exactly to a target, then sorting and concatenating them into one number; combines subset-sum search with digit arrangement, not covered by arrange-digits-to-form-number (which just sorts given digits).
A circular dial pointer turned clockwise/counterclockwise by given amounts; read the landing digit after each turn to build a password. No rotational-dial concept exists in the set.
Tracing a forced knight's-move (L-shape) tour visiting every square once to find which number lands on a marked square.
Simulating soldiers filling road holes (stack/queue behaviour: fill, others pass, climb out to the back) to find the final order; a distinct simulation/logic task.

Using two mirror/projection views of a solid built from different-length blocks to deduce how many of one block type are used; a 3D deduction task distinct from block-count-3d (simple stacked block counting).
Fitting numbered puzzle pieces into blank cells so touching edge colours match (rotation allowed), then reading the answer as a number.
Adding a large number of days to a known weekday and reducing modulo 7 to find the resulting day of week.
Repeated doubling of a quantity until it first exceeds a threshold; distinct from number-line-jumps (equal-sized jumps) since growth is multiplicative.
Comparing total path length made of horizontal/vertical unit segments across picture options.
Using six digit cards to form two 3-digit numbers whose sum is closest to a target, then summing the result's digits; a search/optimization task beyond simple arrange-digits-to-form-number.
Solving pictorial equations (mug total, cup squared) via division/square-root, then adding results.
Evaluating a simple flowchart with an if/else branch on a computed condition; no flowchart/branching concept exists in the set.
Using row/column letter clues on a coordinate grid to locate a unique seat, then evaluating an expression on its coordinates.
A vertical addition where identical shapes represent identical digits; use place-value carries to solve for each shape then sum. Distinct method from the multiplication-digit-puzzle family.
Turning a numbered dial clockwise/counterclockwise by given amounts and recording landing digits to form a password.
Deducing how many cards a player must hold so that all ranks pair off except one designated unpaired card; a set-completion logic task.
Distributing coloured balls of different weights among three people so each gets equal count and equal total weight with distinct colour combinations; solve for one person's count of a colour.
Simulating soldiers filling holes and rejoining the back of the line to find the final order.
Using two mirror views of a solid built from different-length blocks to determine how many unit (white) blocks are used.
Rotating a fixed polyomino (T-shape) cover over a value grid in all orientations/positions to maximise the covered sum; an optimization-search task distinct from rectangle-area-grid.
Inferring a rule from nested-figure examples (reading digits innermost to outermost) and applying it to a new figure; a rule-inference task distinct from visual-pattern-next or custom-operation.
Finding the longest route on a street map without repeating any edge (an Euler-trail style graph problem); not covered by grid-path-steps/maze-path-shortest (shortest-path concepts).
Matching painted area made of quarter-circles plus straight pieces across figure options by counting curved parts and straight area separately.
Solving for a missing figure piece so that painted and white areas of a grid become exactly equal; an area-balancing task distinct from perimeter-area-composed.
Counting how many valid numbers can be formed from given digit cards under parity and range constraints; a combinatorial counting task, not just single-number arrangement.
Computing counts from a data table then finding the median of the sorted counts; a statistics concept absent from the set.
A sequence defined by the absolute difference of the two preceding terms; requires generating terms and detecting a repeating cycle to find a distant term.
Finding the next year reusing the same set of digits (rearranged) as a given year, then computing the year gap.

Each triangle side shows the product of its two vertex values; factor shared products to recover each vertex, then sum. Distinct from combination-product-sum (two numbers from sum/product) since it's a three-vertex factoring deduction.
Distributing balls of three weights among three people with equal count/weight and distinct colour combinations; solve for one person's count of a colour given an extra disambiguating clue.
A long multiplication with several hidden digit boxes; deduce the factors from partial products, then sum all box digits.
Counting distinct tilings of a 3x3 grid using one 1x1 tile and four 2x1 dominoes, using colouring-parity reasoning; a combinatorial tiling task not covered by rectangle-area-grid.
Simulating soldiers filling deep holes (needing two stacked) and rejoining the line to find the final marching order.
Using two mirror views of a solid built from mixed-length blocks to determine the maximum number of unit (white) cubes possible.
Filling 1-9 uniquely into a grid subject to circle-sum (four surrounding squares) and pattern-group-sum constraints, then reading a 3-digit answer from specific cells.
